## Tours Visiting Île Royale: How to Choose an Itinerary

[Île Royale](/french-guiana/place/ile-royale/) lies off the coast of French Guiana in the Îles du Salut archipelago. It is known for its surviving buildings from the former French penal colony. On a walk around the island, historic structures alternate with tropical vegetation and views of the Atlantic Ocean.

The sea crossing is an essential part of choosing a trip. Seeing [French Guiana](/french-guiana/) among the countries on an itinerary does not guarantee a landing on Île Royale. Here you will find routes that include the island as part of their main itinerary.

## Which Itineraries Visit the Island?

[Guianas Adventure](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) is a 9-day journey through Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana, combining the islands' history with a space center, cities, and natural attractions. It suits travelers seeking varied experiences within a relatively compact trip.

[Suriname, Guyana, French Guiana](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) lasts 14 days. Alongside the islands and the coast, it includes substantially more river and nature experiences in Suriname. This itinerary calls for greater readiness for longer transfers and changes of transport.

When comparing the programs, consider not just the length of the entire trip but also the time spent on the coast: how much time is allowed for landing, which neighboring islands are included, and how the day at sea connects to the transfer to Kourou.

## How Île Royale Differs from Saint-Joseph

Île Royale retains prominent structures from the former penal colony. [Île Saint-Joseph](/french-guiana/place/ile-saint-joseph/) lies nearby, but its ruins are more heavily overgrown with tropical greenery, creating a noticeably more secluded atmosphere. Both belonged to the same system, yet exploring each island is a different experience.

The archipelago's third island, [Devil's Island](/french-guiana/place/devils-island/), is known for its history of political exile. Visitors cannot normally land there because of dangerous currents. The appearance of all three islands on a map should therefore not be taken as a promise that all three can be visited.

On the mainland, [Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni](/french-guiana/place/saint-laurent-du-maroni/) continues the historical story with its former transportation camp. Together, these sites provide a fuller understanding of the penal colony than visiting a single location.

## How to Fit the Boat Excursion into Your Trip

Boats depart for the archipelago from the coast around Kourou. Sailings depend on schedules and weather. Check which stops are possible on your chosen day and how much time is set aside to explore the shore and walking paths.

Kourou is also home to the [Guiana Space Centre](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/). Visits follow separate access arrangements, while the opportunity to watch a launch depends on a different schedule. Combining the space center with the islands requires coordinating times; they cannot be treated as one guaranteed excursion.

Bring comfortable shoes, drinking water, and protection from both the sun and rain. Multi-country itineraries also need extra time for transport connections and document checks.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours to Île Royale

### Are Île Royale and Devil's Island the same place?

No. They are separate islands in the Îles du Salut archipelago. Visiting Île Royale does not mean landing on Devil's Island.

### Can I see Île Royale and Saint-Joseph on the same trip?

They are in the same archipelago, but the actual stops depend on sailing conditions and the itinerary. Compare [tours visiting Saint-Joseph](/french-guiana/place/ile-saint-joseph/tour/).

### How many days do I need for a trip that includes Île Royale?

The sea excursion is only one stage of a multi-country journey. Choosing between the 9-day and 14-day itineraries depends primarily on how much time you want to devote to Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana.

## Île Saint-Joseph: Prison Ruins in a Tropical Forest

**Île Saint-Joseph** is one of the three Îles du Salut islands off the coast of [French Guiana](/french-guiana/). Unlike the more developed [Île Royale](/french-guiana/place/ile-royale/), it is particularly known for the remains of a high-security penal colony. Old prison walls and corridors are gradually disappearing beneath tropical vegetation.

Travelers come here chiefly for its history. The beauty of the ocean scenery should not obscure the purpose of the surviving structures: Saint-Joseph was used to isolate prisoners in harsh conditions. Exploring the ruins requires attention to the condition of the old walls and pathways.

## Saint-Joseph's Role in the Colonial Penal System

The Îles du Salut formed part of the French penal colony system. Saint-Joseph housed facilities for strict solitary confinement. Individual blocks, cells, and passageways recall the isolation regime imposed on prisoners.

After the penal system ceased operating, tropical plants gradually took over some of the abandoned buildings. The result is an unusual landscape for a historic site: stone and brick walls still define the outlines of prison courtyards, while roots and leaves push through their openings.

The island's history is best understood as evidence of a particular era rather than the setting of an adventure film. During a guided visit, it is worth asking which rooms served as cells, where the corridors ran, and how Saint-Joseph was connected to the administrative center on Île Royale.

## What to See on a Walk

### Remains of Cells and Prison Blocks

Saint-Joseph's main landmark is the **ruins of the former high-security prison camp**. Surviving walls reveal the layout of cells and passageways. Some structures are badly damaged, and access to certain areas may be restricted.

For safety, do not enter closed rooms or touch unstable masonry. Humidity, tree roots, and time all affect the old structures on this tropical island.

### Walking Paths and the Shore

Footpaths connect the historic structures with the coastline. From the shore, you can see rocky stretches and views of the ocean. Follow the signs and do not attempt to bypass closed sections through dense vegetation.

Saint-Joseph is a destination for a historical walk; safe swimming cannot be promised at every appealing spot. Waves and coastal currents can be strong, and the shoreline is not always suitable for entering the water.

### Views of Neighboring Islands

Saint-Joseph is close to Île Royale and [Devil's Island](/french-guiana/place/devils-island/). The latter remains closed to tourist landings. Seeing it from the water or from permitted viewpoints helps convey the geographical isolation of the former penal colony.

## How to Reach Saint-Joseph

Most boat excursions to the Îles du Salut depart from the **Kourou** area. Travelers generally visit Île Royale first, as it has the archipelago's main visitor facilities. Continuing to land on Saint-Joseph is possible only when conditions allow.

CNES notes that landing facilities on Saint-Joseph are limited and that access depends on waves and currents. Therefore, **an island appearing on the list of stops does not guarantee a landing on any given day**. Before booking an excursion, ask how the operator handles changes in weather.

| Question | Practical Answer |
|---|---|
| Departure point | Kourou area |
| Is landing possible? | Subject to sea conditions |
| Main focus | History of imprisonment |
| What to bring | Water and closed-toe shoes |

Exposed parts of the island can be hot, while forest paths are often damp. Sun protection, a hat, drinking water, and shoes with good grip are useful.

## How Saint-Joseph Differs from Île Royale

**Île Royale** has more substantial surviving historic infrastructure, including museum sites, a chapel, and administrative buildings. On **Saint-Joseph**, the focus is on high-security prison blocks and ruins surrounded by vegetation. The second island presents greater challenges in terms of safety and landing conditions.

Do not expect to walk between all three islands: they are separated by water, and tourist access to Devil's Island is prohibited. The captain determines the boat route between permitted stops.

## Saint-Joseph on an Ada Tours Itinerary

Our [Guianas Adventure](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) tour includes a catamaran excursion to the islands of the former penal archipelago. The itinerary provides for landings on Île Royale and Saint-Joseph, with Devil's Island viewed from the water. The boat excursion occupies a full day.

On the same itinerary, colonial history is combined with contemporary French Guiana and the [Guiana Space Centre in Kourou](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/). It is important to distinguish between the **planned itinerary** and what can actually take place when conditions at sea impose restrictions: weather may affect the island portion of the trip.

For travelers interested in colonial history, another worthwhile stop is [Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni](/french-guiana/place/saint-laurent-du-maroni/), where the former transportation camp reveals a different aspect of the penal system.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Île Saint-Joseph

### Why are there so many ruins on Saint-Joseph?

After the penal colony system closed, the buildings ceased serving their original purpose. They deteriorated, and tropical vegetation gradually reclaimed the grounds.

### Can I visit the island on any day?

No. Landing depends on boat operations, the condition of landing facilities, and conditions at sea.

### How is Saint-Joseph different from Devil's Island?

Tourist visits to Saint-Joseph are possible in favorable conditions. Ordinary tourists are not permitted to land on Devil's Island.

### Is there a museum here?

The main exhibition on the history of the penal colony is associated with Île Royale. Visitors go to Saint-Joseph mainly to explore the ruins and walk around the island.

## Tours Visiting Saint-Joseph: History off the Coast of Kourou

[Île Saint-Joseph](/french-guiana/place/ile-saint-joseph/) belongs to the Îles du Salut archipelago off French Guiana. Ruins of colonial prison buildings survive here among tropical vegetation. The stop is especially rewarding for travelers who want to see historical sites beyond the cities.

Saint-Joseph is visited on a boat excursion from the Kourou area. Traveling through French Guiana does not by itself mean the excursion is included: it must be a dedicated stage of the itinerary.

## Which Tours Include Saint-Joseph?

On the 9-day [Guianas Adventure](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/), the islands' history is combined with Guyana, Suriname, and other stops in French Guiana. This option introduces three territories on a relatively short trip.

The 14-day [Suriname, Guyana, French Guiana](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) journey combines Saint-Joseph with river, city, and nature experiences. Beyond the island, it reaches more remote parts of Suriname, requiring more time on the road and more changes of transport.

Both programs include the island within a much larger journey. Choose according to what interests you elsewhere along the route: cultural and historic sites, tropical forests, rivers, and waterfalls. There is little reason to lengthen the trip solely for one island unless you want those additional experiences.

## Saint-Joseph, Île Royale, and Devil's Island

The archipelago is linked to the history of the French penal colony system, but the islands are not identical. [Île Royale](/french-guiana/place/ile-royale/) retains buildings that make it easier to discover the colony's history. On Saint-Joseph, old brickwork and dense vegetation create a different sense of place.

[Devil's Island](/french-guiana/place/devils-island/) is known for its history of political exile, but standard tourist landings are not possible because of dangerous currents. This explains why an itinerary may mention the archipelago without visiting all three islands.

To compare the history of imprisonment on the islands with that of the mainland, consider including [Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni](/french-guiana/place/saint-laurent-du-maroni/) and its former transportation camp. There, the historical context emerges from the town's buildings and its location on the Maroni River.

## What to Arrange Before Traveling

The main questions concern whether landing will actually be possible, how long you can explore, sea conditions, and the local boat operator's arrangements. Even when the overall itinerary works well, the crossing is weather-dependent. Closed-toe shoes, water, a hat, and light rain protection are useful for exploring the ruins and paths.

The [Guiana Space Centre in Kourou](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/) is on the mainland near the boat departure area, but access to the space center is arranged separately. Watching a rocket launch depends on mission schedules; it should not be combined with a Saint-Joseph visit as a guaranteed single-day activity without checking.

A longer trip through the Guianas also calls for coordination of connections, border crossings, and documents. We can help plan the sequence, but the exact content of the island excursion is determined by the confirmed itinerary.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Visiting Saint-Joseph

### Can I see Saint-Joseph and Île Royale on the same day at sea?

It depends on sailing schedules and weather. Check the actual program for the combination you want, rather than relying only on the name of the archipelago.

### Is the island suitable for a regular beach vacation?

The main reasons to visit are the historic ruins and natural scenery. Conditions at sea should not be compared with those of a developed beach resort.

### Should I choose the 9-day or the 14-day itinerary?

Nine days suit a more compact introduction to the three Guianas. Fourteen days allow for more river and nature stops beyond the island portion.

## Places to Visit in French Guiana: From Cayenne to the Amazon

[French Guiana](/french-guiana/) differs from its neighbors on South America's northern coast: it is an overseas territory of France where tropical nature meets European administrative institutions and a space center. The main destinations for travelers are [Cayenne](/french-guiana/place/cayenne/), the [Guiana Space Centre in Kourou](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/), the Îles du Salut, and the river regions of the Guianan Amazon.

We have brought together {{catalog.placesCountPhrase}} here. When choosing where to go, consider the available transport: a city visit, an island boat trip, and an expedition into remote rainforest require very different amounts of time and preparation.

## Cayenne: A Creole City and Starting Point

[Cayenne](/french-guiana/place/cayenne/) is a good place to begin exploring the territory. In its central neighborhoods, you can see colorful wooden facades, Place des Palmistes, old houses, and markets selling local produce. The city's cuisine reflects a mix of Creole, European, and other cultural traditions.

Allow time to explore the center separately from a trip to the spaceport. Humidity and heat affect the pace, so plan daytime outings around the sun and possible showers. When choosing a city tour, check whether it covers only the streets or also includes museums and other indoor sites.

## Kourou and the Space Center

The [Guiana Space Centre](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/) is one of the most unusual places to visit in South America. It stands near the Atlantic coast and is linked to European space programs. There is an important distinction between touring selected space center facilities, visiting a museum, and watching an actual launch: each has different access rules.

Launches follow operational schedules and may be postponed. Even an announced launch date does not guarantee that travelers will see a launch or gain access to their preferred viewing area. Check the official calendar, entry permit rules, and possible restrictions on movement well in advance.

The Kourou area can be visited on a separate day from Cayenne. When schedules allow, the trip can be combined with a boat excursion to the islands.

## The Îles du Salut: The History of a Former Penal Colony

Off the coast of Kourou lie the Îles du Salut, islands associated with the French penal colony system. Among the places that tourists can visit are [Île Royale](/french-guiana/place/ile-royale/) and [Saint-Joseph](/french-guiana/place/ile-saint-joseph/). Buildings and traces of former infrastructure survive on both. Their appeal combines colonial history with natural coastal scenery.

Devil's Island is often mentioned alongside them, but **it should not automatically be considered open for landing**: the French tourism portal specifically describes restrictions on visiting the island. Before booking a boat excursion, confirm where the vessel actually stops, which landings are possible, and what can be seen ashore.

Boat trips depend on wind and waves. For a historical visit, it is better to allow sufficient time on land than to choose only the shortest possible crossing.

## The Amazon and Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni

The [French Guiana Amazon Rainforest](/french-guiana/place/french-guiana-amazon-rainforest/) offers another kind of journey. Here, the main attractions are tropical forests, rivers, and local communities. Some areas have no roads, so travel may depend on boats and domestic flights. Such journeys need separate planning, including access regulations and local guiding arrangements.

[Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni](/french-guiana/place/saint-laurent-du-maroni/) stands on the Maroni River and is known for its former transportation camp. It offers a different perspective on the colonial period and appeals to travelers interested in regional history. Paying attention to weather and river transport is just as important here as planning museum visits.

| Place | Main Reason to Visit |
|---|---|
| Cayenne | Culture and markets |
| Kourou | Space center |
| Îles du Salut | Penal colony history and the sea |
| Amazon rainforest | Nature and river journeys |

## Choosing the Season and Preparing for Your Trip

Tropical rainfall in French Guiana follows a seasonal pattern. The French tourism portal identifies a comparatively drier period, roughly July to November, as convenient for some outdoor activities. This does not guarantee rain-free weather. For island excursions, sea conditions and confirmed departures matter; for rainforest travel, rainfall, water levels, and restrictions on the specific route are important.

Bring lightweight sun-protective clothing, a raincoat, non-slip footwear, and waterproof protection for documents. Entry and medical requirements depend on nationality and itinerary. Because French Guiana is not the same as metropolitan France, check the current rules specifically for this territory.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Places in French Guiana

### Can I combine Cayenne and the Kourou spaceport on a short trip?

Yes. Both are accessible by road, but you need to allow for driving time and the space center's visiting schedule.

### Can I land on Devil's Island?

Regular tourist programs do not provide for unrestricted landings. Check which islands are accessible and the boat's actual itinerary; Île Royale and Saint-Joseph are the more common stops.

### Can I explore deep into the French Guiana Amazon on my own?

Remote regions often require specialist arrangements and local guides. Before choosing a route, check transport availability, protected-area rules, and seasonal conditions.

## Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni: A Border Town with Penal Colony History

**Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni** is located on the western border of [French Guiana](/french-guiana/), on the Maroni River. The Surinamese town of Albina stands on the opposite bank. Routes between the two countries of the Guianas cross the river here.

Two distinct themes make the town worth exploring: the history of the French penal colony system and life at a border where the river is both a transport route and an international boundary. You can discover both on one walk, although crossing the river requires separate border formalities.

## The Former Transportation Camp: The Main Historic Landmark

Saint-Laurent's best-known site is **Camp de la Transportation**, the former transportation camp. Prisoners passed through this colonial system of punishment and assignment. The complex retains brick buildings, courtyards, and other elements of an institution whose history spans the 19th and 20th centuries.

Today, part of the site serves cultural and museum purposes. The former camp houses the **Centre d'Interprétation de l'Architecture et du Patrimoine (CIAP)**, which offers guided tours, exhibitions, and educational events. The local authorities confirm that the center operates within Camp de la Transportation itself.

A visit helps explain Saint-Laurent's place in the penal system and lets you compare its history with that of the island colony in the Îles du Salut. On [Île Royale](/french-guiana/place/ile-royale/) and [Saint-Joseph](/french-guiana/place/ile-saint-joseph/), structures from a different part of the same system survive.

## What to See in Town

### Camp Architecture and the Historic Center

A typical visit begins with the buildings of the former camp. The surrounding neighborhoods have brick and wooden buildings, elements of the administrative heritage, and streets associated with the town's growth along the riverbank.

Make time for an explanation of the architecture. Without a guided historical account, the former camp might look simply like a group of old buildings, although its history is far more complex.

### The Banks of the Maroni River

The river reveals contemporary life in the border region. Boats carry freight and passengers, and the opposite bank already belongs to Suriname. A river outing and an international crossing are different activities. The presence of a boat does not mean you can cross the national border without having your documents checked.

### Cultural Life at the Former Camp

Camp de la Transportation also serves as a public space today. Depending on the program, exhibitions and cultural events may take place here. Before visiting, check the opening hours of individual rooms and the availability of guided tours.

## Crossing the Border into Suriname

Routes from **Albina**, on the Surinamese bank, use boats to cross the Maroni. Yet the two towns' geographical proximity does not remove immigration and departure procedures: appropriate documents are required, and the applicable rules depend on nationality and itinerary.

Our current itinerary includes crossing the border by local boat and completing the border formalities. For travelers, it is important to coordinate transport, arrival times, and the document-checking process.

| Stage | What to Consider |
|---|---|
| Albina | Departure from Suriname |
| River crossing | Boat and luggage |
| Saint-Laurent | Entry into French Guiana |
| Historic center | Time for a guided visit |

French Guiana is an overseas region of France. Its entry rules may differ from those for travel to metropolitan France. Before departure, check the latest official requirements for your nationality and route; an ordinary Schengen visa should not be assumed to grant automatic entry.

## Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni on Ada Tours Itineraries

On our [Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana tour](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/), the group crosses the river from Albina, learns about the former penal system, and continues toward [Cayenne](/french-guiana/place/cayenne/) and Kourou.

The [Guianas Adventure](/multi-country/tour/guianas-adventure/) also includes the river crossing and a visit to Saint-Laurent. Both are combined itineraries across several territories, so compare the order of border crossings, transport arrangements, and length of individual days when choosing.

A visit to the former transportation camp pairs well with a boat trip to the Îles du Salut and a visit to the [Guiana Space Centre in Kourou](/french-guiana/place/guiana-space-centre/). These sites tell different historic and modern stories of the same region.

## When to Plan Your Trip

French Guiana has a humid tropical climate and heavy rainfall in certain months, especially during the first half of the year. Weather affects walking comfort, road travel, and river traffic. Bring drinking water, a hat, and light clothing for hot weather, and rain protection for wet conditions.

If your route includes a border crossing, allow extra time for formalities. Arriving in Saint-Laurent too late may leave insufficient time for a guided visit to the historic complex.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni

### What is the town known for?

Its former transportation camp within the French penal colony system and its position on the Suriname border beside the Maroni River.

### Can I visit the transportation camp?

Yes. The complex is used as a heritage and cultural site. Check with the local CIAP for available tour formats and access to specific rooms.

### Where is Albina?

On the opposite, Surinamese bank of the Maroni. Boat services operate between the towns, subject to border procedures.

### Is a regular Schengen visa enough for the trip?

Do not automatically assume it is sufficient. Entry requirements for French Guiana depend on nationality and document status and must be checked against official regulations.
